subject.title: security fix(gateway): defend pre-auth device-signature verify against CPU DoS

question: Should OpenClaw accept this PR's new pre-auth device-signature input caps and per-IP fail-closed rate-limit gate as the Gateway security boundary?
rationale: This changes unauthenticated Gateway auth behavior and protocol validation in a way that improves DoS resistance but can also reject previously tolerated oversized device fields or lock out device-bearing clients earlier under shared-IP abuse.

options.title: Accept the new boundary
options.body: Approve the protocol caps and device-signature bucket as the desired security posture, then land after normal exact-head checks.

options.title: Request narrower compatibility proof
options.body: Require exact regression coverage or docs for token-bearing lockout reasons and over-bound client behavior before merge.

options.title: Replace with unified auth gate
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers want all pre-auth credential throttling moved into a different shared owner boundary instead.

recommendation.title: Accept the new boundary
recommendation.body: Approve the protocol caps and device-signature bucket as the desired security posture, then land after normal exact-head checks.

likelyOwner.reason: Best available decision owner from the reviewed history because they merged the sibling bootstrap-token auth limiter fix and were explicitly routed for review in this PR discussion.
